channel.title: Management Review · Stiven Catalyst
channel.description: Management without theatre, to listen to. Every episode is a conversation about one issue of the Management Review, the monthly magazine of Stiven Catalyst: what the research says about leading people and operations, and what to do with it on the next shift. The episodes are made with AI (NotebookLM) from the text of each issue; the figures, their sources and the tools are in the issue, free on stivencatalyst.com.

item.itunes:title: Why great employees make bad managers
item.description: Management Review No. 01: What the best managers do. Ten behaviours from Google's research, why the talent to manage is rare, and how a team can rate its own manager. Correction, 14 October 2026. Four passages the issue does not support were cut from this recording, 24 seconds in all: that the manager explains engagement “entirely”, and that “the environment, the pay, the perks” make up the other 30% (Gallup found that the manager explains at least 70% of the differences between business units, and says nothing about the rest); that technical skill is “only 10% of the recipe” and the rest 90% (one of Google’s ten behaviours is technical: a count, not a share); and that “9 out of 10 people are not built for this” (according to Gallup, 1 in 10 have high talent to manage, and 2 in 10 more have basic talent). Each episode is made with AI (NotebookLM) from the text of one issue: two voices talk the issue through. They can simplify, and now and then get something wrong; the issue is the reference, with every figure and its source. Read the issue: https://stivencatalyst.com/magazine/management-review-nr-01.html
